issue.title: bug: `:%s/` can crash Neovim with `lua-language-server` after #13243

repository.name: neovim

issue.body:
### Problem

I'm not too familiar with how to get a stack trace and/or attach a debugger, but the repro should be reliable.

I suspect this has to do with the edge case of updating multiple locations at once. Though I'm not sure what the role of the LSP is (I suppose it's just for creating extmarks and it's probably possible to reproduce without LSP).

I'm using `RelWithDebInfo`.

Bisected #13243 @bfredl 

### Steps to reproduce

1. Checkout https://github.com/llllvvuu/neovim/tree/25155-repro
2. `nvim --noplugin --clean -u minimal.lua runtime/lua/vim/shared.lua`, where `minimal.lua` is:
```lua
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('FileType', {
  pattern = { 'lua' },
  callback = function()
    vim.lsp.start({
      name = 'lua_ls',
      cmd = {'lua-language-server'},
      root_dir = vim.fs.dirname(vim.fs.find({'.git', '.luacheckrc' }, { upward = true })[1]),
    })
  end,
})
```
3. Try to do: `/Node<CR>V3j:s/Node/Tree`. Neovim should crash when you type the first letter of "Tree".

### Expected behavior

Whether or not the LSP is proper or malformed, Neovim should handle it gracefully.

### Neovim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.10.0-dev-1089+g1c4a93b59

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

NVIM v0.10.0-dev-1089+g1c4a93b59

### Operating system/version

13.4.1

### Terminal name/version

kitty 0.28.1

### $TERM environment variable

xterm-kitty

### Installation

build from repo

issue.title: fix(marktree): off-by-one error in `marktree_move`

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
If you would insert element X at position j, then if you are moving that
same element X from position i < j, you should move it to position j -
1, because you are losing an element.
    
This error caused a gap to be left in the array, so that it looked like
[x, null, y] instead of [x, y], where len = 2. This triggered #25147.
    
Fixes: #25147
